meta.title: Two Diaries, One Sunday
meta.textType: functional: two diary pages on one day (two texts to compare)

paragraphs: On Monday, January eleventh, Mom had a plan for the family book. "Can you write a diary page about Sunday?" she asked Lily and Tom. She wanted one page from each of them. Each page had a name and the date at the top: Sunday, January tenth. Lily's page had a drawing of the lake. Lily's page began, "Dear diary, we left at eight o'clock." Tom's page began, "Dear diary, we left at eight o'clock." The two pages began in the same way.

Lily wrote, "We went to the lake with Dad and Pip." "The morning was cool, so we wore jackets." "I sat on a mat and drew the lake." "Dad sat under a big tree with a thermos." "Pip ran after a duck along the water." "The duck was fast." Tom wrote, "It was a cool morning, and I wore my jacket." "I stood at the side of the lake with my fishing rod." "I have loved fishing since I was small." "I fished for two hours, and I caught nothing." "The water was very quiet." "It was a good day, too."

Lily wrote, "At lunch time, we sat under the big tree." "I made a sandwich myself, and Dad liked it." "Pip lay beside the picnic box." "The sandwich was good." Tom wrote, "We ate lunch under the big tree." "After lunch, I lay down on the grass with my jacket under my head." "I did not move for ten minutes." "I was pleased that Dad came with us."

Lily wrote, "I like being outdoors, but I hate the cold wind." "The wind came from the lake." "In my opinion, the lake is best in the morning." "I have wanted a picnic since last week." Tom wrote, "I did not like the worms." "I like a cool day, and it was not as hot as last Sunday." "My usual Sunday is at home, so this day was special." "It was a good day."

Lily ended, "Tomorrow, I will tell Mia about the duck, and I hope that we go again." Tom ended, "I want to try a new place, and I will not forget my hat." Dad read both pages and said, "Let us decide next Sunday." "Do you agree that the lake is best in the morning?" Lily asked Tom. "Yes, I agree," said Tom, "but next time I will catch a fish." Mom smiled at the two pages.
text.summary: Lily and Tom each write a diary page about the same Sunday at the lake. The pages say some of the same things and some different things, and Dad says the family will decide on the next trip.
